title: Client request coalescing benchmark scratch
content:
Purpose:
Quick scratchpad for client-side request coalescing experiments. Goal: measure tradeoffs when doing small-window coalescing at the client/edge before hitting Redwood API vs. server-side batching only. Focus on p50/p95/p99 changes under mixed arrival patterns and how it affects token/sec and GPU utilization.

Experiment summary (high level):
- System under test: Redwood hosted API (dev-stage cluster), model: rw-medium-8k-quant (approx representative).
- Client-side coalescer implemented in ingress proxy (repo PR linked above). Simple strategy: buffer incoming requests for up to W ms or until N requests queued, then send a multiplexed request to server. Server treats as multiple independent requests and expands.
- Sweeped W in {0, 5, 10, 20, 50} ms and N in {2,4,8}. Arrival patterns: Poisson low (10 rps), steady medium (150 rps), bursty spike (sawtooth: baseline 50 rps with 500rps 1s spikes every 30s), and real-client blend (replay trace subset).

Repro commands (approx):
- loader: ./tools/loadgen --profile=poisson --rps=150 --trace=short-replay.json --payload=short-prompt.json --threads=32 --duration=600
- coalescer config: /etc/ingress/conf/coalesce.json {"window_ms": 10, "max_batch": 4}
- metrics: prometheus job 'ingress', 'redwood-api', and local loadgen logs (latency buckets).

Key measurements (selected):
ASCII table shows p50/p95/p99 (ms) and throughput (token/s) for sawtooth spike workload:
W_ms | N | p50 | p95 | p99 | token/s | error%
-----+---+-----+-----+-----+---------+------
0    | 1 | 42  | 120 | 380 | 28.5k  | 0.03
5    | 4 | 55  | 140 | 430 | 31.8k  | 0.04
10   | 4 | 68  | 165 | 560 | 34.0k  | 0.06
20   | 8 | 92  | 230 | 780 | 36.2k  | 0.09
50   | 8 | 150 | 420 | 1500| 37.1k  | 0.22

Observations (raw):
- Small windows (5-10ms) increase overall tokens/sec by ~10-20% compared to no client coalescing. This comes from better packing of network and small-KV cache hits (more amortized decoder calls).
- p99 tail grows more than p95 for larger windows, especially under short spikes. Example: 50ms window pushes p99 into seconds for some requests (see spike events at t=120s).
- Error rate climbs slightly for larger N due to request multiplexing edge bugs (race on timeout flush). Filed JIRA-ENG-2147 to track bug.
- Under low Poisson load (10 rps) coalescing gives negligible throughput benefit and introduces fixed latency penalty (coalesce wait). Not worth it for low-util clients.
- Under steady medium load coalescing 5-10ms with N<=4 looks like the best sweet spot: modest latency increase at p50 (~+10-20ms) for sizable throughput gain and GPU efficiency increase (observed on metrics).

Micro-notes (trace-level):
- Looking at ingress traces, coalesced requests show a microburst at server inbound (larger batch) but server runtime kernel selection handles bursts well; however KV cache pressure increases p99 when many different prefixes are coalesced together. A follow-up: try prefix-aware coalescing (group by hashed conversation id).
- When we ran mixed client types (some clients coalescing, some not), the heterogeneity reduced benefits: non-coalesced requests still create many small kernels, so benefit diluted. Consider per-tenant policy enforcement if we want uniform gains.

Quick artifacts (what I saved):
- loadgen logs: /tmp/load-runs/2025-11-03-coalesce-sawtooth.tar.gz
- Prom dashboard snapshots: grafana/dashboard/snap-2025-11-03-coalesce.png
- Ingress proxy trace example (span id): trace:0x8f3c21 (attached in PR thread)

Quick conclusions / action items:
- For edge coalescing, recommend default ON with conservative params (W=5ms, N=4) for medium/large tenants where baseline RPS>50. Add server-side metric to detect negative tail regressions.
- Add prefix grouping to client coalescer to avoid mixing unrelated contexts (experiment next).
- Fix race on flush/error path (JIRA-ENG-2147) before broader rollout.
- Add A/B test: 10% of traffic with coalescer W=20ms (canary) for 2 days to capture production tails.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How does coalescing interact with request-level function-calling / tool calls? Need to ensure tool call ordering preserved when multiplexed. Quick test planned: replay tool-call heavy trace with N=2, W=5ms.
- Need more GPU-level metrics (SM utilization per-ptx) to quantify kernel amortization. Ask infra team for finer telemetry.
- Determine per-tenant heuristics (should we disable for small tenants?).

Notes to self (messy):
- saw a couple of 5-6s p99s in run-7; likely due to a timeout cascade (ingress waited for buffer, backend slow on that specific shard). Keep an eye on shard mapping.
- If we do prefix grouping, consider consistent hashing by tenant+conversation modulo 64 to avoid head-of-line blocking.

End of scratchpad. Revisit after PR fixes and run the planned A/B canary.

Signed: Alyssa (quick notes, will formalize if results hold)
